subject: MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate and GitHub MCP Server stateless support

selection.reason: The base protocol lifecycle changes one day before the scheduled final release, affects production MCP scaling and state design, and is inspectable in a normative release candidate, official SDK, conformance suite, and GitHub server source.

signals.note: Reviewed recent OpenAI, Anthropic, Google/DeepMind, GitHub developer-tool, vLLM, and NVIDIA announcement surfaces.
Reviewed accessible X search signals around Claude Opus 5, MCP, and NVIDIA Korea; no X content is used as article evidence.

alternatives.subject: Claude Opus 5 availability in GitHub Copilot
alternatives.reason: Recent availability is confirmed, but GitHub performance language is vendor testing and did not provide enough same-condition independent evidence for a stronger technical conclusion.

alternatives.subject: NVIDIA and Korea AI infrastructure partnerships
alternatives.reason: Highly relevant to Korean readers, but the latest material is mainly partnership and capacity announcements without an inspectable new hardware or software artifact for a software-engineering decision.

alternatives.subject: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless core and GitHub server support
alternatives.reason: Normative text, immutable code, an official SDK prerelease, and executable conformance tests support a scoped engineering conclusion.

conflicts: GitHub is the publisher and operator of the GitHub MCP Server being described.
The Model Context Protocol project and official SDK maintainers describe their own specification and implementations.
No advance access, vendor account, credits, sponsorship, or embargo was provided.

claims.claim: The MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate removes the initialize/initialized handshake and protocol-level session, moves version and client capability metadata to each request, and adds server/discover.
claims.method: Compared the official RC explanation, draft specification, and immutable RC release tag.

sources.limitations: Maintainer explanation of an unreleased final specification.
Mutable draft URL; final text may differ.
Release candidate explicitly permits changes before final.

limitations: The final 2026-07-28 specification had not shipped at article time.
Protocol statelessness does not eliminate application state.
conflict_of_interest: Specification authors are describing their own protocol revision.

claims.claim: GitHub announced support for the next MCP specification, and its public server commit configures a stateless Streamable HTTP handler and depends on the official Go SDK v1.7.0-pre.3.
claims.method: Inspected go.mod and pkg/http/handler.go at immutable GitHub MCP Server commit eb088dfe9d854dab6453a8d4ae5871a5ced20974.

sources.limitations: Vendor announcement; no hosted deployment metrics or source revision is supplied.
Public repository may not match the hosted service deployment.
Dependency declaration alone does not prove hosted conformance.

limitations: No GitHub hosted-server conformance result was published.
No latency, database-operation, or scaling benchmark artifact was published.
conflict_of_interest: GitHub describes and maintains its own server.
recheck_triggers: GitHub publishes an exact hosted revision or conformance report
A stable GitHub MCP Server release pins the final protocol SDK

claims.claim: Teams should separate protocol state from application state and verify version negotiation, fallback, authorization, idempotency, and observability independently during migration.
claims.method: Derived from the protocol's explicit-handle design, SDK compatibility boundaries, and conformance workflow.

sources.limitations: Protocol-level guidance does not validate organization-specific controls.
Conformance does not replace application security and workload testing.
